answer: Public audit trails can make sybil clones expensive by logging each agent's transaction graph and flagging suspiciously synchronized behavior—near-identical timing, matching counterparties, mirrored trade sizes. If a hundred "independent" identities all buy saffron futures within the same second and route through the same jade-certified reef of intermediaries, auditors can correlate them into one cluster and downweight its influence. This raises the cost of maintaining convincing sock puppets. What it does not solve: a patient attacker who randomizes behavior across months, or honest.
